last_run_summary: App run 2026-10-28: 0 IRB issue(s), 9 FR docs. score 3: 0, score 2: 0, score 1: 1, score 0: 8; nothing above score 1.
notes: Backfilled ~30 days for the seed run only. Weekly runs are incremental from last_fedreg_date. Dedup by document number absorbs date overlap. Scheduling: Monday 19:00 CET (~1 PM US Eastern) so it catches that Monday's US-morning IRS / Federal Register release. FR FULL-TEXT WORKAROUND (updated 2026-09-30): the FR API full_text_xml_url and full_text/text URLs are now ALSO redirected to the unblock.federalregister.gov bot-check (failed for 2026-17781). Working alternative: WebFetch https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-<YYYY-MM-DD>/html/<doc_number>.htm (publication date in the path) - returns full text (confirmed again 2026-10-25 for 2026-21715); use it to check which forms a PRA notice bundles (guard's 'form named in a core bucket -> cap at 1' rule) or to pull a DATES block when comments_close_on is null (e.g. 2026-18645 had null comments_close_on but DATES said 2026-11-10; the FR API documents/<doc>.json?fields[]=dates field also surfaced it). IRB NPRMs often reference FR docs published before the FR window - match via FR API conditions[term] search and label 'match not verified' unless the REG number is confirmed. IRB pages are very large (100k-450k chars) and WebFetch truncates at 100k: use offset=100000 follow-ups or the PDF (irs.gov/pub/irs-irbs/irb26-NN.pdf) if completeness matters. IMPORTANT lesson from 2026-08-24: for any FinCEN/Treasury final rule touching an ownership/entity-transparency/AML regime, the FR abstract can describe only one part of a multi-part holding - before scoring such a final rule 0 or 1, do a quick WebSearch for news coverage of the document number as a sanity check. If a run crosses midnight, re-pull the FR from the prior date so the new last_fedreg_date bookmark doesn't skip a day.
